title: Star-Cursed Lovers: Role of Popularity Information in Online Dating
eligible_reason: Treatment is a user's displayed popularity star rating (1/2/3 stars) that changes up and down over time; estimated with ordered logit and FE ordered logit (clogit/suest) of received preference ratings on star1/star3 indicators. Multi-valued, non-absorbing treatment, nonlinear main models, no staggered binary adoption.
design_notes: Tables.do: Table 4 ologit g_pref_r on star1_r star3_r (with/without profile controls) and a fixed-effects ordered logit (Baetschmann-style clogit + suest over cutoffs, sample max_star_r != min_star_r & n_r<100); message-sending logits (Table 5); Appendix A1 linear OLS/xtreg FE counterparts (xtreg g_pref_r star1_r star3_r, fe). Star status switches between 1, 2 and 3 within user; no calendar-time FE, no adoption cohorts.
data_files_note: Data.dta (816,992 rater-ratee-game rows, 16,552 ratees) described as 'a subset of our original data'; the appendix FE regression comment reports 630,160 obs, consistent with the analysis sample.
data_provenance_note: Subset of the platform data with the analysis variables; no noise or synthetic generation stated.
software_notes: Stata do-files with Windows (CR) line endings.
screener_notes: No article text or PDF available locally (data/text and papers/ empty for this suffix); screened from README, code, data and the OpenAlex abstract. Popularity-information design with a multi-valued switching treatment; not DiD.
